what: Photo panels are joined in a single line (horizontal or vertical) and flow endlessly with wheel or drag inside a perspective-tilted cluster (WebGL). Each panel sags sideways by cos(t × .18) × bend − bend according to its axis distance t, and recedes by |t|^1.25 × depth, so the band curves like a bow. The wheel adds deltaY × .18 to the velocity (±180), which cools by .92 per frame, and each frame pushes by .005 × velocity × .52. Two name lines on each panel (data-top · data-bottom) sit tilted clockwise at 32° and 12°, blur as the flow speeds up (velocity ÷ 14), and return by .28 per frame when it stops. When the category changes, the visible panels blur out and drop away at .09s stagger over .28s, the whole set blurs by 10px, and then the new panels rise from .88x at .055s stagger over .52s power3.out.

options.axis: x (horizontal strip, default) · y (vertical strip — detail page)
options.size-y: Board box height, default 1.28 — the wide band is fitted inside the box by ratio
options.pos: Cluster position x,y,z, default -.9,.1,.32 (portrait .72,0,.35 — below width 1400 .6→.15, below 767 0)
options.[data-fx-part=item]: One panel (hidden) — data-ratio (width/height) · data-label · data-tone=dark|mid · data-video · data-top·data-bottom (two name lines) · data-category · data-href (click to go)
options.Event: fx:filter on panel { category } Firing it keeps only that category (all keeps everything) · the vertical strip fires fx:bend-strip-gl when the center panel changes { index }

note: The original uses WebGPU node materials (three r184) — the same bend formula was ported to a WebGL shader. Name letters are a letter panel instead of the original three-text (real 3D letters), and like the original it inherits the photo panel’s ratio (.72×1.28) and stretches vertically. The wheel is received on the whole window, so a panel covering one screen is used
